name: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
title: Seal of the Prophets
bio: The final Messenger of Allah, born in Mecca around 570 CE. He received the first revelation at the age of 40 and led the Muslim community from Mecca to Medina until his passing in 632 CE.

name: Prophet Adam
title: The First Man
bio: The first human being and the first prophet, created by Allah from clay. He and his wife lived in Paradise before being sent down to the earth.

name: Prophet Idris
title: The Truthful
bio: Mentioned in the Quran as a truthful prophet whom Allah raised to a high station.

name: Prophet Nuh
title: The Ark Builder
bio: Called his people to worship Allah alone for 950 years, according to the Quran. By Allah's command he built the ark that saved the believers from the flood.

name: Prophet Hud
title: Messenger to Ad
bio: Sent to the people of Ad, a mighty nation who rejected his call and were destroyed by a violent wind.

name: Prophet Salih
title: Messenger to Thamud
bio: Sent to the people of Thamud, who were given a miraculous she-camel as a sign. They harmed her and were struck by punishment.

name: Prophet Ibrahim
title: Khalilullah, Friend of Allah
bio: Rejected the idols of his people and was tested with great trials. With his son Ismail he raised the foundations of the Kaaba.

name: Prophet Lut
title: Warner of His People
bio: Sent to a people who committed grave sins. He and his family, except his wife, were saved when the punishment came.

name: Prophet Ismail
title: True to His Promise
bio: Son of Ibrahim, described in the Quran as true to his promise. He helped his father build the Kaaba in Mecca.

name: Prophet Ishaq
title: Blessed Son of Ibrahim
bio: Son of Ibrahim and father of Yaqub, given as glad tidings to his parents in their old age.

name: Prophet Yaqub
title: The Patient Father
bio: Son of Ishaq and father of Yusuf and his brothers. He showed beautiful patience when he lost his son Yusuf.

name: Prophet Yusuf
title: The Interpreter of Dreams
bio: Betrayed by his brothers and imprisoned unjustly, he was given knowledge of dream interpretation and rose to authority in Egypt.

name: Prophet Ayyub
title: The Patient
bio: Tested with severe illness and loss, he remained patient and turned to Allah, who restored his health and blessings.

name: Prophet Shuayb
title: Messenger to Madyan
bio: Sent to the people of Madyan, whom he urged to worship Allah alone and to deal honestly in weights and measures.

name: Prophet Musa
title: Kalimullah, Spoke with Allah
bio: The prophet most often mentioned in the Quran. He confronted Pharaoh and led the Children of Israel out of Egypt.

name: Prophet Harun
title: Helper of Musa
bio: The brother of Musa, whom Allah appointed as his helper and spokesman.

name: Prophet Dhul-Kifl
title: The Patient and Righteous
bio: Mentioned in the Quran among the patient and the righteous servants of Allah.

name: Prophet Dawud
title: King and Prophet
bio: Received the Zabur and was given wisdom and kingship. As a young man he defeated the tyrant Jalut (Goliath).

name: Prophet Sulayman
title: The Wise King
bio: Son of Dawud, granted a unique kingdom by Allah, including authority over the wind and understanding of the speech of birds.

name: Prophet Ilyas
title: Opponent of Idolatry
bio: Called his people to leave the worship of Ba'l and to worship Allah alone.

name: Prophet al-Yasa
title: Among the Chosen
bio: Mentioned in the Quran among the chosen and the best of people.

name: Prophet Yunus
title: Dhun-Nun, Companion of the Fish
bio: Swallowed by a great fish after leaving his people. In the darkness he glorified Allah and was saved.

name: Prophet Zakariyya
title: Guardian of Maryam
bio: Cared for Maryam and prayed for a child in his old age. Allah answered him with the gift of Yahya.

name: Prophet Yahya
title: The Pure
bio: Son of Zakariyya, given wisdom and purity from his youth, and known for his devotion and kindness.

name: Prophet Isa
title: Al-Masih, Son of Maryam
bio: Born miraculously to Maryam and sent to the Children of Israel with the Injil. He performed miracles by Allah's permission.

name: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq
title: The Truthful, First Caliph
bio: The closest companion of the Prophet ﷺ, who accompanied him during the Hijrah. He became the first caliph (632-634 CE) and held the community together after the Prophet's passing.

name: Umar ibn al-Khattab
title: Al-Faruq, Second Caliph
bio: Second caliph (634-644 CE), known for his strict justice. Under his leadership the state expanded greatly and many administrative systems were established.

name: Uthman ibn Affan
title: Third Caliph
bio: Third caliph (644-656 CE), known for his modesty and generosity. He oversaw the creation of standard written copies of the Quran.

name: Ali ibn Abi Talib
title: Fourth Caliph
bio: Cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet ﷺ, and one of the first to accept Islam. Famed for his courage, knowledge and eloquence, he was the fourth caliph (656-661 CE).

name: Khalid ibn al-Walid
title: Sayfullah, the Sword of Allah
bio: A brilliant military commander who never lost a battle after accepting Islam. He led decisive campaigns in Iraq and Syria, including the Battle of Yarmouk.

name: Hamza ibn Abdul-Muttalib
title: Lion of Allah
bio: Uncle of the Prophet ﷺ and one of the bravest warriors of Quraysh. He fought at Badr and was martyred at the Battle of Uhud in 625 CE.

name: Khadija bint Khuwaylid
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: The first wife of the Prophet ﷺ and a successful merchant. She was the first to believe in his message and supported him through the hardest years in Mecca.

name: Aisha bint Abi Bakr
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: A wife of the Prophet ﷺ and a renowned scholar. She narrated a large number of hadiths and taught many students after the Prophet's passing.

name: Fatima az-Zahra
title: Daughter of the Prophet
bio: The youngest daughter of the Prophet ﷺ and wife of Ali. She is the mother of Hasan and Husayn and is remembered for her piety and patience.

name: Bilal ibn Rabah
title: The First Muadhdhin
bio: Born into slavery, he endured torture in Mecca for refusing to abandon his faith. He was freed by Abu Bakr and became the first caller to prayer in Islam.

name: Abu Hurayra
title: Narrator of Hadith
bio: A companion who stayed close to the Prophet ﷺ in Medina and became one of the most prolific narrators of hadith.

name: Abdullah ibn Abbas
title: Interpreter of the Quran
bio: Cousin of the Prophet ﷺ, known as the scholar of the Ummah for his knowledge of Quranic interpretation. He was still young when the Prophet ﷺ passed away.

name: Al-Hasan ibn Ali
title: Grandson of the Prophet
bio: The elder grandson of the Prophet ﷺ. After his father's death he gave up the caliphate to unite the Muslims.

name: Al-Husayn ibn Ali
title: Grandson of the Prophet
bio: The younger grandson of the Prophet ﷺ, martyred at Karbala in 680 CE (61 AH).

name: Salman al-Farisi
title: The Seeker of Truth
bio: A Persian companion who travelled far in search of the truth. He suggested digging the trench that protected Medina during the Battle of the Trench in 627 CE.

name: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas
title: The Archer of Islam
bio: One of the earliest Muslims and among the ten promised Paradise. He commanded the Muslim army at the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah against the Persian Empire.

name: Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah
title: Trustworthy of the Ummah
bio: One of the ten promised Paradise, known for his honesty and humility. He led the Muslim armies in the conquest of Syria.

name: Az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam
title: Disciple of the Prophet
bio: A cousin of the Prophet ﷺ and one of the ten promised Paradise. He was a fearless horseman who fought in nearly all the major battles of the era.

name: Talha ibn Ubaydullah
title: The Shield at Uhud
bio: One of the ten promised Paradise. At the Battle of Uhud he shielded the Prophet ﷺ and suffered many wounds defending him.

name: Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf
title: The Generous Merchant
bio: One of the ten promised Paradise and a gifted trader who built a fortune in Medina. He gave very large sums in charity and for the defense of the community.

name: Abdullah ibn Umar
title: Follower of the Sunnah
bio: Son of Umar, famed for closely following the example of the Prophet ﷺ and for narrating many hadiths.

name: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud
title: Teacher of the Quran
bio: One of the earliest Muslims and among the most knowledgeable companions in the Quran. He later taught the people of Kufa.

name: Anas ibn Malik
title: Servant of the Prophet
bio: Served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years from his childhood in Medina and narrated many hadiths.

name: Mu'adh ibn Jabal
title: Knower of Halal and Haram
bio: A young companion from Medina whom the Prophet ﷺ praised for his knowledge of the lawful and the forbidden, and sent to teach in Yemen.

name: Zayd ibn Thabit
title: Scribe of the Revelation
bio: A young scribe of the Prophet ﷺ who led the collection of the Quran in written form after the Prophet's passing.

name: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari
title: The Truth-Teller
bio: An early convert known for his honesty, simple living and plain speech.

name: Umm Salama
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: A wife of the Prophet ﷺ, known for her wisdom and the sound advice she gave at Hudaybiyyah. She migrated to Abyssinia and later to Medina.

name: Mus'ab ibn Umayr
title: The First Ambassador
bio: Raised in comfort in Mecca, he gave up wealth for his faith. He was sent to Medina to teach Islam before the Hijrah and was martyred carrying the banner at Uhud.

name: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib
title: Leader of the Migration to Abyssinia
bio: Cousin of the Prophet ﷺ and spokesman of the Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia. He was martyred at the Battle of Mu'tah in 629 CE.

name: Amr ibn al-As
title: Conqueror of Egypt
bio: A skilled commander and strategist who led the Muslim conquest of Egypt around 640 CE and founded the city of Fustat.

name: Ammar ibn Yasir
title: Steadfast in Hardship
bio: An early convert who endured severe persecution in Mecca together with his parents, Yasir and Sumayyah. He remained a loyal companion until his death at Siffin in 657 CE.

name: Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman
title: Keeper of the Secrets
bio: A companion trusted by the Prophet ﷺ with knowledge about the hypocrites. He was sent on a night mission during the Battle of the Trench.

name: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari
title: Host of the Prophet
bio: The Medinan companion in whose house the Prophet ﷺ first stayed after the Hijrah. He kept fighting in the way of Allah into old age.

name: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh
title: Leader of the Aws
bio: Chief of the Aws tribe in Medina and a strong supporter of the Prophet ﷺ. He died from a wound received at the Battle of the Trench.

name: Sumayyah bint Khayyat
title: The First Martyr
bio: An early Muslim woman of Mecca who endured torture for her faith and is remembered as the first martyr in Islam.

name: Asma bint Abi Bakr
title: She of the Two Belts
bio: Daughter of Abu Bakr who brought food and supplies to the Prophet ﷺ and her father during the Hijrah. She is known as Dhat an-Nitaqayn.

name: Nusayba bint Ka'b
title: Defender at Uhud
bio: Also known as Umm Ammara, a brave woman of Medina who fought to protect the Prophet ﷺ at the Battle of Uhud.

name: Hafsa bint Umar
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: A wife of the Prophet ﷺ and daughter of Umar. She kept the written copy of the Quran compiled under Abu Bakr.

name: Ubayy ibn Ka'b
title: Master of Reciters
bio: A companion from Medina and scribe of the Prophet ﷺ, named among the best reciters of the Quran.

name: Muhammad al-Fatih
title: Conqueror of Constantinople
bio: Ottoman sultan who conquered Constantinople in 1453 CE at about the age of 21.

name: Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi
title: Liberator of Jerusalem
bio: Founder of the Ayyubid dynasty. After the victory at Hattin he recaptured Jerusalem in 1187 CE and was admired for his chivalry and mercy.

name: Tariq ibn Ziyad
title: Conqueror of Al-Andalus
bio: An Umayyad general who crossed into the Iberian Peninsula in 711 CE. His campaign began the Muslim rule of Al-Andalus.

name: Sayf ad-Din Qutuz
title: Victor of Ain Jalut
bio: Mamluk sultan who defeated the Mongol army at the Battle of Ain Jalut in 1260 CE.

name: Baibars
title: Sultan of the Mamluks
bio: A commander at Ain Jalut who later became Mamluk sultan and recovered many strongholds from the Crusaders.

name: Uqba ibn Nafi
title: Founder of Kairouan
bio: Umayyad commander who led conquests in North Africa and founded the city of Kairouan around 670 CE.

name: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim
title: Young General of Sindh
bio: A young Umayyad commander who led the conquest of Sindh around 711 CE.

name: Yusuf ibn Tashfin
title: Victor of Zallaqa
bio: Almoravid leader who crossed into Al-Andalus and defeated Alfonso VI at the Battle of Zallaqa in 1086 CE.

name: Omar al-Mukhtar
title: Lion of the Desert
bio: Libyan teacher of the Quran and resistance leader who fought Italian colonial rule for over twenty years until his execution in 1931.

name: Emir Abdelkader
title: Emir of the Algerian Resistance
bio: Algerian scholar and leader who resisted the French conquest of Algeria from 1832 to 1847.

name: Nur ad-Din Zangi
title: Unifier of Syria
bio: Ruler of Syria who united Muslim lands against the Crusaders and paved the way for Salah ad-Din.

name: Musa ibn Nusayr
title: Governor of Ifriqiya
bio: Umayyad governor of North Africa who oversaw the expansion into the Maghreb and the conquest of Al-Andalus.

name: Imam Abu Hanifa
title: Imam of the Hanafi School
bio: Al-Nu'man ibn Thabit (d. 767 CE), founder of the Hanafi school and a leading jurist of Kufa and Baghdad.

name: Imam Malik ibn Anas
title: Imam of Medina
bio: Founder of the Maliki school (d. 795 CE) and author of the Muwatta, one of the earliest collections of hadith and fiqh.

name: Imam ash-Shafi'i
title: Founder of Usul al-Fiqh
bio: Muhammad ibn Idris ash-Shafi'i (d. 820 CE), founder of the Shafi'i school and author of ar-Risala on the principles of jurisprudence.

name: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
title: Imam of Ahl as-Sunnah
bio: Founder of the Hanbali school (d. 855 CE) and compiler of the Musnad. He was imprisoned and tortured for refusing to say that the Quran is created.

name: Imam al-Bukhari
title: Compiler of Sahih al-Bukhari
bio: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (d. 870 CE), whose Sahih is regarded as the most authentic collection of hadith.

name: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Sheikh al-Islam
bio: Hanbali scholar (d. 1328 CE) who wrote extensively on creed and jurisprudence and defended the way of the Salaf.

name: Imam Muslim
title: Compiler of Sahih Muslim
bio: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj (d. 875 CE), author of Sahih Muslim, the second most revered collection of hadith.

name: Abu Dawud as-Sijistani
title: Author of Sunan Abi Dawud
bio: Hadith scholar (d. 889 CE) who compiled the Sunan, with a focus on hadiths of legal rulings.

name: Imam at-Tirmidhi
title: Author of Jami at-Tirmidhi
bio: Hadith scholar (d. 892 CE) who compiled the Jami, noting the grades of hadiths and the views of the jurists.

name: Imam an-Nasa'i
title: Author of Sunan an-Nasa'i
bio: Hadith scholar (d. 915 CE) known for his strict conditions in accepting narrators.

name: Imam Ibn Majah
title: Author of Sunan Ibn Majah
bio: Hadith scholar from Qazvin (d. 887 CE) whose Sunan is counted among the six major collections.

name: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Student of Ibn Taymiyyah
bio: Hanbali scholar (d. 1350 CE) famed for his works on the heart and on Prophetic guidance, such as Zad al-Ma'ad.

name: Ibn Kathir
title: Mufassir and Historian
bio: Scholar (d. 1373 CE) who wrote a famous commentary on the Quran and the history al-Bidaya wa'n-Nihaya.

name: Adh-Dhahabi
title: Historian of Scholars
bio: Scholar (d. 1348 CE) known for Siyar A'lam an-Nubala and his works on hadith narrators and Islamic history.

name: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
title: Commentator of Sahih al-Bukhari
bio: Hadith scholar (d. 1449 CE) who wrote Fath al-Bari, the best-known commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari.

name: Abd al-Aziz ibn Baz
title: Grand Mufti of Saudi Arabia
bio: Scholar (1912-1999 CE) who served as Grand Mufti of Saudi Arabia and was known for his teaching and fatwas.

name: Muhammad Nasir ad-Din al-Albani
title: Scholar of Hadith
bio: Scholar (1914-1999 CE) born in Albania and known for his work in grading hadiths.

name: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
title: Scholar of Hadith and the Heart
bio: Hanbali scholar (d. 1393 CE), author of Jami' al-'Ulum wa'l-Hikam, a commentary on forty hadiths.

name: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi
title: Author of al-Mughni
bio: Hanbali jurist (d. 1223 CE) who wrote al-Mughni, a major work of comparative jurisprudence.

name: Ibn Abd al-Barr
title: Hafiz of Al-Andalus
bio: Maliki scholar of Al-Andalus (d. 1071 CE), known for at-Tamhid and al-Isti'ab on the companions.

name: Sufyan ath-Thawri
title: Leader of the Hadith Scholars
bio: Early scholar of Kufa (d. 778 CE), a leading hadith narrator and jurist known for his piety.

name: Imam al-Awza'i
title: Imam of the Levant
bio: Scholar of Syria (d. 774 CE) whose legal school was followed for a time in the Levant and Al-Andalus.

name: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak
title: Scholar and Mujahid
bio: Scholar of Khurasan (d. 797 CE), known for his knowledge of hadith, his generosity and his service on the frontiers.

name: Muhammad ibn Salih al-Uthaymeen
title: Scholar of Unayzah
bio: Scholar (1929-2001 CE) from Qassim in Saudi Arabia, known for his teaching and his explanations of fiqh and creed.

name: The First Revelation
title: The Cave of Hira
bio: In the cave of Hira near Mecca, around 610 CE, the angel Jibril brought the first verses of the Quran to the Prophet ﷺ, beginning with the command "Read" (Iqra).

name: The Night Journey and Ascension
title: From Mecca to Jerusalem and the Heavens
bio: In a single night, before the Hijrah, the Prophet ﷺ was taken from the Sacred Mosque in Mecca to al-Aqsa in Jerusalem, then ascended through the heavens. The five daily prayers were prescribed on this journey.

name: The Migration to Abyssinia
title: Refuge Under the Negus
bio: Around 615 CE a group of persecuted Muslims left Mecca for Abyssinia, where the just king an-Najashi gave them protection. Ja'far ibn Abi Talib spoke for them before the king.

name: The Second Pledge of al-Aqaba
title: The Pledge of Medina
bio: Shortly before the Hijrah, a delegation from Medina pledged at al-Aqaba, near Mecca, to protect the Prophet ﷺ as they would protect their own families, which opened the way to the migration.

name: The Hijrah
title: Migration to Medina
bio: In 622 CE the Prophet ﷺ left Mecca with Abu Bakr and sheltered in the cave of Thawr before reaching Medina. This migration marks the start of the Hijri calendar, introduced later under Umar.

name: Battle of Badr
title: The Day of Criterion
bio: Fought in Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE), the first major battle of Islam. Around 313 Muslims faced a Qurayshi army about three times larger and won a decisive victory.

name: Battle of Uhud
title: The Lesson of Obedience
bio: Fought in 3 AH (625 CE) near the mountain of Uhud, north of Medina. The Muslims were close to victory until a group of archers left their post. Hamza was martyred in this battle.

name: Battle of the Trench
title: The Siege of Medina
bio: In 5 AH (627 CE) a coalition of tribes besieged Medina. On the advice of Salman al-Farisi the Muslims dug a trench around the exposed side of the city, and the siege failed.

name: Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
title: The Clear Victory
bio: In 6 AH (628 CE) the Prophet ﷺ and Quraysh agreed to a ten-year truce near Mecca. The treaty looked unfavorable to many Muslims, but the Quran called it a clear victory, and it paved the way to the conquest of Mecca.

name: Battle of Khaybar
title: The Fortresses of the North
bio: In 7 AH the Muslims marched against the fortified settlements of Khaybar, an oasis north of Medina, and took them after a campaign that lasted several days.

name: Battle of Mu'tah
title: The Three Commanders
bio: In 8 AH (629 CE) a small Muslim army met a far larger Byzantine force. Zayd ibn Haritha, Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and Abdullah ibn Rawaha were martyred in turn, and Khalid ibn al-Walid took command and saved the army.

name: Conquest of Mecca
title: The Great Opening
bio: In 8 AH (630 CE) the Prophet ﷺ entered Mecca with a large army almost without fighting. The idols around the Kaaba were removed, and he forgave the people of Quraysh.

name: Battle of Hunayn
title: The Valley Between Mecca and Ta'if
bio: Soon after the conquest of Mecca, the Muslims faced the tribes of Hawazin and Thaqif in the valley of Hunayn. They were shaken at first, then regrouped around the Prophet ﷺ and won.

name: Expedition of Tabuk
title: The Army of Hardship
bio: In 9 AH (630 CE) the Prophet ﷺ led a large army north in the heat of summer to face Byzantine forces. No battle took place, but the expedition showed the strength of the Muslim state.

name: The Farewell Pilgrimage
title: The Sermon at Arafat
bio: In 10 AH (632 CE) the Prophet ﷺ performed his only Hajj and gave his farewell sermon at Arafat, stressing the sanctity of life and property and the rights of all people before Allah.

name: Battle of Yamama
title: War Against the False Prophet
bio: Fought in 632-633 CE under Abu Bakr against the followers of Musaylima, who claimed to be a prophet. Many reciters of the Quran fell, which led to the first written compilation of the Quran.

name: Battle of Yarmouk
title: Decisive Victory in the Levant
bio: In 636 CE the Muslim army under Khalid ibn al-Walid and Abu Ubayda defeated a much larger Byzantine army by the Yarmouk river, opening the way for the conquest of the Levant.

name: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah
title: The Fall of the Sasanian Frontier
bio: Around 636 CE the Muslim army led by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas defeated the Sasanian Persian army in Iraq after several days of fighting, a turning point in the conquest of Persia.

name: Battle of Guadalete
title: The Gate to Al-Andalus
bio: In 711 CE Tariq ibn Ziyad defeated the Visigothic king Roderic in southern Iberia, a victory that started the Muslim presence in Al-Andalus.

name: Battle of az-Zallaqa
title: The Almoravids Cross the Strait
bio: In 1086 CE Yusuf ibn Tashfin crossed from North Africa to help the Andalusian rulers and defeated the army of Alfonso VI of Castile near Badajoz.

name: Battle of Hattin
title: Road to Jerusalem
bio: In 1187 CE Salah ad-Din crushed the Crusader army near Tiberias. Jerusalem was recaptured a few months later without a massacre.

name: Battle of Ain Jalut
title: The Mongols Are Stopped
bio: In 1260 CE the Mamluk army under Qutuz, with Baibars among its commanders, defeated the Mongols in Palestine, ending their advance toward Egypt.

name: Conquest of Constantinople
title: The Prophecy Fulfilled
bio: In 1453 CE the Ottoman sultan Muhammad al-Fatih took Constantinople after a siege of about 53 days, ending the Byzantine Empire and fulfilling a long-awaited hope of the Muslims.
